This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #33356: Same root cause — unbounded `event` table growth dominated by `message.updated.1` full snapshots per streaming update, reaching 13 GB+, with source-level analysis and the same proposed fixes (compact superseded snapshots, store deltas, add pruning).
- #38362: Related — OOM crash caused by the same `event` table snapshot accumulation plus an unbounded `revert` column, with identical mitigation suggestions.

Confirmed duplicate of #37617 / #33788 — same symptom on Desktop 1.18.15 (Windows 11): the Settings → General "Auto-accept permissions" toggle stays disabled (`not-allowed`), never persists a value.

Also confirmed the workaround from #37617 works: pressing **Ctrl+Shift+A** (Mod+Shift+A) inside an active chat toggles auto-accept for the current session — the runtime feature works fine, only the Settings UI entry is broken.

Please track this under #37617 / #33767. Closing this one is fine; keeping it open just for visibility on 1.18.15.

Another reproduction of the same bug family on the latest production build — Windows 11, Desktop **1.18.15**:

1. Deleted the project folder from disk (after quitting the app).
2. Recreated a folder with the **same name**.
3. The old sessions for that project reappeared in the new project's session list — session data is evidently keyed by project name/path, not by folder identity.

This is the same symptom described in #41068 (which the bot flagged as a duplicate of this issue). Just adding the fresh 1.18.15 repro data here so it stays tracked on this issue. Happy to provide logs/screenshots if needed.

Confirming overlap with #31401 (already tracked, assigned to Hona): the "recreating a same-named folder brings back old sessions" part is exactly #31401. I've added fresh 1.18.15 reproduction details there so the data lives on the officially tracked issue.

The UI-level "no delete option for sessions/projects" part of this report overlaps #40786 / #33129 / #38771 — worth keeping those open for the UX-side fix even if this one gets closed as duplicate. Tracking this issue here as the umbrella for both angles is fine.

Could a maintainer reopen? I can rebase onto the latest dev if needed.

- **Closes #35329** (a Windows-only bug: `@parcel/watcher` emits backslash paths on Windows, but the rest of the codebase compares/stores paths with forward slashes, so watcher event paths never matched anything — file ops, `@file` mentions, cache keys, etc.).

One additional observation: if I manually trigger OpenCode to update/refresh the current session, the TODO sidebar starts working correctly and the task statuses update incrementally as expected. This suggests that the underlying TODO state may already be updated during execution, but the sidebar UI is not being refreshed or re-rendered until a session update is triggered. Once the session is refreshed, completed tasks are immediately reflected correctly.

Same symptom here, and I can add strong evidence that this is a zen/go serving-path defect, not a client issue.

Timeline
- Started 2026-08-07 evening (UTC+8), right after the opencode-go provider informed me they completed a local deployment of the DeepSeek V4 Flash lane and updated usage billing.
- Reproduces on opencode 1.18.15 AND after downgrading to 1.18.14 — same behavior. Not a client version regression.
- Upgrading the magic-context plugin (0.34.1 → 0.34.2) changed nothing.

Observed pattern (matches your analysis exactly)
- The stopped responses always end with a colon — the model finished its text and was about to emit tool calls, then the response ended with finish_reason: stop and zero tool calls.
- From our local message store (opencode DB), the failed turns show:
  - finish: stop with output tokens as low as 19–61 (normal turns in the same session produce 100–1400 output tokens and finish: tool-calls)
  - several turns show finish: None / output: 0 (stream ended without a proper finish marker)
- It is intermittent: in the same long-running session, ~60–80% of turns complete with tool calls, then a turn "says what it will do" and stops.
- It correlates with very long conversations: all failures happened at 254k–281k context tokens; the same model in a fresh/short session does not exhibit it.

What I ruled out
- Not a tool failure: proofloop MCP tools return success on adjacent turns.
- Not permission/ask: no permission prompts on those turns.
- Not client timeout/abort: no AbortError in logs for these turns; the stream simply ended with finish_reason: stop.

Please prioritize the streaming text→tool_calls transition in the zen/go serving path. A control run against api.deepseek.com with the same prompt/tools completes tool calls 4/4, so the model itself is fine.

Additional findings from further analysis (confirmed on Windows desktop 1.18.15):

1. **The error sound is only ever played in response to a live `session.error` event** (see `packages/app/src/context/notification.tsx` → `handleSessionError`). Persisted notifications are **not** replayed with sound on startup — so the 3 beeps heard right after launching the app must come from **3 live events emitted during the startup phase**.

2. In our logs, the startup phase (`03:05:12Z`–`03:05:50Z` on 2026-08-08: config load → LSP bootstrap → location services → `init count=120`) contains **no ERROR lines at all** (no `failed to load plugin`, no `server unavailable` — those were fixed earlier). Yet the user still heard 3 error sounds. This means the 3 `session.error` events come from a path that **does not write an ERROR log line**, so they are invisible in `opencode.log`.

3. That combination — audible error sounds with zero log footprint and zero UI indicator — is exactly why an Error/Diagnostics viewer is needed: it would make the event source visible regardless of the log-writing path.

Repro hints for maintainers: Windows desktop app, multiple MCP servers + plugins configured, launch the app while the previous session/tab is restored. If helpful, I can collect a full log bundle (`logs.export`) and attach it.

Issue: feature request for a centralized error viewer plus surfacing error notifications in the UI (not sound-only).

I tested this against the reported `0.0.0-next-16783` build with an isolated home/config directory.

A global config containing only the native V2 `mcp.servers` shape is loaded on a fresh service boot; the configured server appears in `GET /api/mcp` as expected. I was able to reproduce the empty MCP list when the same global document mixed a legacy config key (for example, singular `plugin`) with native `mcp.servers`. That build classified the whole document as V1 and consequently omitted the native MCP section. Project config appeared to work because the control document was native-only. Mixed V1/V2 config normalization has since been fixed on the current V2 branch.

There is a separate config hot-reload gap: MCP currently snapshots config when a location's services boot and does not reconcile MCP servers after config changes. That can make an edit appear ignored until the location/service is recreated, but it does not prevent native config-file servers from loading at initial boot.

Given the exact-version reproduction above, the reported startup failure is stale/misdiagnosed rather than an MCP startup-registration bug. If a native-only global config still fails on a current build, please share the redacted `opencode2 debug config` output so we can compare the effective config source and normalized document.

All of these describe the same core symptom: `deepseek-v4-flash` failing on `opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` while other models on the same key/endpoint succeed. Following up — same symptom as reported here (HTTP failure on `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` for `deepseek-v4-flash`, other models on the same key/endpoint still 200). Adding two new data points that I don't see in this thread yet:

**1. The 400 / 500 / "Model is unavailable" responses are transport-dependent (Anthropic vs OpenAI wire), not just server-side fluctuation.**

I ran both endpoints against the **same** Go subscription key, **same** account, **same** machine, **seconds** apart:

| Wire | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions | `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` | **HTTP 400** `Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: Model is unavailable.` |
| Anthropic Messages | `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` | **HTTP 200** full chat completion, `model: deepseek-v4-flash`, `stop_reason: max_tokens` |

So the `zen/go` host is currently serving deepseek-v4-flash on the Anthropic wire (`/v1/messages`) but rejecting the same request on the OpenAI-compatible wire (`/v1/chat/completions`). That's not a hang or rate-limit — it's a per-wire routing-level failure on the host that Anomaly routes Flash through.

**2. The official OpenCode CLI gets it right because it doesn't use Console Go for this model.**

`opencode.exe run -m opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash "hi"` returns a valid response immediately after the same `chat_completions` call returns 400. Internal logger:

```
message=stream providerID=opencode-go modelID=deepseek-v4-flash llm.runtime=ai-sdk
```

So the CLI's opencode-go provider is reaching DeepSeek through a different upstream path than the `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. The CLI path is the one that's currently healthy; the public HTTP `chat_completions` route is the one that's broken.

**Implication for downstream clients**

Third-party OpenAI-compatible callers (Hermes, custom scripts, CI bots, anything that hits the Go subscription via the documented `chat/completions` endpoint) are all blocked on the same wire, even though the model itself is up and the same account is happily serving via the CLI. Commenting here since this thread has the most concentrated community signal — same model, same endpoint, same failure window.

Thanks for the note. I believe this is a distinct issue from #31041.

In this case, the OPTIONS preflight is **not** failing — it returns `200` with proper CORS headers:
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type, Authorization`, `access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS` (verified via curl).

The problem is that the **actual GET/POST response** (e.g. `/zen/go/v1/models`) does **not** include `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` at all:

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models" -H "Origin: http://localhost:8000/" HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json Server: cloudflare

<-- no access-control-* header on the actual response

Even after a successful preflight, browsers still validate the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on the actual response. Since it is missing, the request is blocked with a CORS error ("Failed to fetch"). A same-origin server-side proxy works around it, which confirms the root cause.

So: #31041 covers the preflight (OPTIONS 404) problem, while this issue covers the missing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` on actual responses. I'd suggest keeping them separate, or merging #31041 into this one if the maintainers prefer a single CORS tracking issue.

**Root cause + verified fix: Luna on Go is Responses-API-only**

Checked the duplicates (#33942, #39831, and #40420 — same underlying transport issue from a Hermes consumer). The common thread: `gpt-5.6-luna` is the *only* Go model served via the OpenAI **Responses API** — the [Go endpoint table](https://opencode.ai/docs/go#endpoints) lists it at `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses` with `@ai-sdk/openai`, not chat/completions. Anything through `/chat/completions` then misbehaves: images → silent empty `message` (this issue), text → missing `finish_reason` (#40420).

Verified working — image via the Responses route:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "input": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "input_text", "text": "Describe this image."},
      {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}
    ]}]
  }'
```

Returns a normal `output[].content[].output_text` with `status: completed` — so the #40420 `finish_reason:null` class disappears too. We run this from Hermes Agent's aux vision slot in production today.

`models.dev`'s declared `image` modality is accurate — the issue is the transport mismatch. Suggest: return a descriptive error (or proxy to the Responses backend) when `gpt-5.6-luna` gets image parts on chat/completions, instead of the silent empty 200.
I am planning to implement this on a fork. Will make a PR later.
